title: Stationary-start cover-time lower bound
formal: For every irreducible reversible discrete-time Markov chain on n≥2 states, is E_π C≥(n−1)∑_{j=1}^{n−1}1/j?
definitions: A chain is specified by an n×n matrix P of nonnegative real entries whose rows sum to one. Irreducibility means for any i,j some t≥0 has (P^t)_{ij}>0. Its unique stationary probability vector π has positive coordinates and satisfies πP=π. Reversibility means π_i P_ij=π_j P_ji for every pair. Self-loops are permitted and periodic chains are included. Draw X_0 from π and evolve according to P. C=min{t≥0:{X_0,…,X_t}={1,…,n}} counts transitions, so the initial state is already visited at time zero. Expectation includes the random initial state. This is the finite-n exact inequality, not a statement only about the leading n log n term.

context: Aldous and Fill distinguish this stationary-start extremal conjecture from a related asymptotic theorem for unweighted graph walks.
why: An exact extremal bound would identify how quickly a reversible exploration process can cover its state space.

import_provenance.original_statement: Does every irreducible discrete-time reversible Markov chain on n states satisfy Eπ[C]≥(n−1)H_{n−1}, where the walk starts in stationarity and C is the time to visit all states? This exact bound would strengthen the extremal cover-time line in which Feige established the asymptotic n log n lower bound for unweighted graphs.
